## Experimental logic

ChIP-seq measures enrichment of protein-associated DNA fragments. Input controls estimate background from chromatin accessibility, mappability, and library biases.

## Peak types

This workshop focuses on narrow peaks typical of transcription factors or sigma-factor-like binding. 
Histone marks may require broad peak methods and different interpretation.

## Coding Pitfalls

- Wrong genome
- Wrong type of expected peaks affecting peak calling
- Filtering proper reads

## Experimental problems

- Low signal to noise
- Chip-seq that did not produced enrichments leads to low number of recovered peaks and little recovery of mapped reads within peaks.
- Low quality Chip-seq present a high phantom peak in strand cross-correlation (when peak offset  match exactly the sequencing read length)
- Contaminants
